title: Quietam Nox - audiovisual monitoring in children with and without respiratory diseases
summary:
Many children experience breathing problems, especially during sleep. The current standard examination in a sleep laboratory (polysomnography) is complex and can be burdensome for children. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate a new contact-free technology for monitoring breathing during sleep.
The system records breathing movements and breathing sounds without physical contact by using specialized audio, camera, and temperature sensors. A prototype has already been successfully tested on technical models and mannequins. In this study, the technology will now be assessed in children with regard to its usability and feasibility. The investigation will take place in the hospital setting and, potentially, later in the home environment. The aim is to evaluate the potential of a simple and low-burden method for monitoring breathing in children.
The start of the inpatient study component, has been delayed due to the continued pending provision of the required technical equipment by the company. As of 22 June 2026, the required device is still not available for the Ulm site and is not expected to become available in the foreseeable future.

interventions.name: Children who are hospitalized due to a medical indication and their parents who are offered this additional application observation. The application records the child's breathing and is intended to capture, store, and analyze respiratory symptoms during the child's sleep.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age between 6 months and 5 years
- Consent of the legal guardian for the application observation in the clinic or in the outpatient area
Exclusion criteria:
none
